notes.body:
Hi @SYN-bit - I'm having an issue with the original commit for some reassembly. It looks to be spinning/spending a lot of time in `find_and_mark_frame_depended_upon` since the added recursion. 

To trigger this, open the pcap (requires TLS decryption) and add a filter `http2`. This may work the first time (although will take a long time for the size of the pcap`. Clear the filter and add it again and for me Wireshark hangs.

If I remove the recursion in `find_and_mark_frame_depended_upon` it'll work but no idea if this is desired.

[http2-wireshark-img.pcap](/uploads/06cdce971516a16d01ac7a8c87393581/http2-wireshark-img.pcap)
[http2-wireshark-img.keys](/uploads/85e051621044961a8de06d986e974b81/http2-wireshark-img.keys)

Hi @ryandoyle, Thank you for your testing and report. I can reproduce your issue, so I'll put this MR on hold for now, I'll try to figure out what the issue is. I'm away for a long weekend, so it might take some time.
Cheers, Sake
See !9538 which should fix the problems with excess recursion.
This plus cherry-picking !9538 and !9622 should either all go in together (or else close the request.) I think with all three we have ironed out the wrinkles and it would be fine.

Hi @johnthacker (and @desowin), thanks for your additional work on the fix for nested dependent packets. I added your commits and started the pipeline. Could you approve this MR when the pipeline is succesful?
